# certutil

```go
import "github.com/effective-security/xpki/v2/certutil"
```

Package certutil provides utilities to work with certificates.

A Bundler builds and verifies certificate chains. It trusts only the roots it is given, plus the platform trust store when WithSystemRoots\(true\) is set; without trust roots it defaults to Force, which checks signatures only. AIA downloads \(WithAIA\) are bounded by the WithHTTPClient timeout and the context given to BundleContext. One Bundler can be shared by goroutines; intermediates it learns over AIA are reused by later calls:

```
b, err := certutil.NewBundler(nil, intermediates,
	certutil.WithSystemRoots(true),
	certutil.WithAIA(true),
)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
chain, err := b.BundleContext(ctx, []*x509.Certificate{leaf}, nil)
```

<a name="BundleExpiringBit"></a>Warning code for a success

```go
const (
    BundleExpiringBit      int = 1 << iota // 0x01
    BundleNotUbiquitousBit                 // 0x02
)
```

<a name="KeyTypeRSA"></a>Key type names reported by KeyInfo.Type, as crypto/x509 prints the public key algorithm.

```go
const (
    // KeyTypeRSA is the KeyInfo.Type of an RSA key.
    KeyTypeRSA = "RSA"
    // KeyTypeECDSA is the KeyInfo.Type of an ECDSA key.
    KeyTypeECDSA = "ECDSA"
    // KeyTypeMLDSA is the KeyInfo.Type of an ML-DSA (FIPS 204) key.
    KeyTypeMLDSA = "ML-DSA"
)
```

## func [BuildBundle](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundle.go#L85>)

```go
func BuildBundle(c *Chain) (bundle *Bundle, status *BundleStatus, err error)
```

BuildBundle returns the Bundle and BundleStatus of a Chain built by a Bundler. A nil c or c.Cert returns an error; a nil c.Status is treated as an empty status, and a nil c.Root \(a Force chain\) leaves RootCert and RootCertPEM empty \(XPKI\-042\).

<a name="CreateOCSPRequest"></a>
## func [CreateOCSPRequest](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/ocsp.go#L298>)

```go
func CreateOCSPRequest(crt, issuer *x509.Certificate, hash crypto.Hash) ([]byte, error)
```

CreateOCSPRequest returns the DER encoded OCSP request for crt issued by issuer, hashing the issuer key with hash. A nil crt or issuer or an unavailable hash returns an error before any work \(XPKI\-103\), and so does an issuer whose subject is not crt's issuer name or whose key did not sign crt \(XPKI\-121\). The signature check accepts SHA\-1 and applies no CA policy.

<a name="CreateOCSPResponse"></a>
## func [CreateOCSPResponse](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/ocsp.go#L92>)

```go
func CreateOCSPResponse(issuer, responderCert *x509.Certificate, template ocsp.Response, signer crypto.Signer) ([]byte, error)
```

CreateOCSPResponse returns a DER encoded OCSP response signed by signer, the key of responderCert, as ocsp.CreateResponse does: template gives the content, and template.Certificate, when set, is embedded. Unlike ocsp.CreateResponse it also signs with an ML\-DSA key, from any provider: the response is encoded by golang.org/x/crypto/ocsp, and the signature over its tbsResponseData \(RFC 6960 §4.2.1\) is pure ML\-DSA with an empty context and the id\-ml\-dsa\-\* algorithm without parameters \(RFC 9881\). template.SignatureAlgorithm is ignored for an ML\-DSA key, whose parameter set fixes the algorithm. A nil issuer, responderCert or signer, or an uninitialized ML\-DSA key, is an error.

An ML\-DSA response can be read by ParseOCSPResponse and by OpenSSL 3.5, but golang.org/x/crypto/ocsp cannot verify it.

<a name="GetKeyDERFromPEM"></a>
## func [GetKeyDERFromPEM](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/pem.go#L340>)

```go
func GetKeyDERFromPEM(in []byte, password []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

GetKeyDERFromPEM parses a PEM\-encoded private key and returns DER\-format key bytes, decrypting it with password when it is encrypted. Encrypted PKCS\#8 keys are supported only with PBES2, PBKDF2 \(HMAC\-SHA1, \-SHA224, \-SHA256, \-SHA384 or \-SHA512, at most 10,000,000 iterations\) and AES\-128/192/256\-CBC, which OpenSSL 3 writes by default. Other PKCS\#8 schemes \(PBES1, PKCS\#12 PBE, scrypt, DES\) return an "unsupported PKCS\#8 encryption" error \(XPKI\-043\). The decrypted bytes are returned only when they are a PKCS\#8 PrivateKeyInfo; otherwise, as for bad padding, the error matches x509.IncorrectPasswordError \(XPKI\-115\).

<a name="IsPostQuantumCertificate"></a>
## func [IsPostQuantumCertificate](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/pqc.go#L82>)

```go
func IsPostQuantumCertificate(crt *x509.Certificate) bool
```

IsPostQuantumCertificate reports whether crt carries a post\-quantum public key or is signed with a post\-quantum signature algorithm, so a chain that mixes classical and ML\-DSA keys is detected at either end. A nil certificate is not post\-quantum.

<a name="IsPostQuantumKey"></a>
## func [IsPostQuantumKey](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/pqc.go#L47>)

```go
func IsPostQuantumKey(key any) bool
```

IsPostQuantumKey reports whether key is a post\-quantum \(ML\-DSA\) key: an \*mldsa.PublicKey or \*mldsa.PrivateKey, or a crypto.Signer or crypto.Decrypter, such as an HSM or KMS key, whose Public\(\) is one. A nil key is not post\-quantum.

<a name="ParseOCSPResponse"></a>
## func [ParseOCSPResponse](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/ocsp.go#L213>)

```go
func ParseOCSPResponse(der []byte, issuer *x509.Certificate) (*ocsp.Response, error)
```

ParseOCSPResponse parses and verifies a DER encoded OCSP response that holds one status, as ParseOCSPResponseForCert with no certificate.

<a name="ParseOCSPResponseForCert"></a>
## func [ParseOCSPResponseForCert](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/ocsp.go#L234>)

```go
func ParseOCSPResponseForCert(der []byte, cert, issuer *x509.Certificate) (*ocsp.Response, error)
```

ParseOCSPResponseForCert parses a DER encoded OCSP response and returns the status of cert, as ocsp.ParseResponseForCert does, and also verifies a response signed with ML\-DSA, which that function cannot. A response with an embedded certificate is verified with that certificate's key and, when issuer is set, the certificate with the issuer's key; without one, the response is verified with the issuer's key when issuer is set. With no embedded certificate and no issuer the signature is not checked. A status other than successful is an ocsp.ResponseError in the error chain, and a signature that does not verify an ocsp.ParseError, for ML\-DSA too. Response.SignatureAlgorithm is x509.MLDSA44, MLDSA65 or MLDSA87 for an ML\-DSA response, so Response.CheckSignatureFrom works on it.

Like golang.org/x/crypto/ocsp, it does not check that an embedded certificate is authorized to answer for the issuer \(the OCSP signing EKU of RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2\) or is within its validity, or that the CertID names the issuer: any certificate the issuer signed can sign an accepted response. Those checks are left to the service that relies on the result \(ROADMAP item 11\).

```go
func ParsePrivateKeyDER(keyDER []byte) (key crypto.Signer, err error)
```

ParsePrivateKeyDER parses a PKCS \#1, PKCS \#8, ECDSA, Ed25519 or ML\-DSA DER\-encoded private key. The key must not be in PEM format. An ML\-DSA key must be in the PKCS \#8 seed form \(RFC 9881\), which x509.MarshalPKCS8PrivateKey and "openssl genpkey \-provparam ml\-dsa.output\_formats=seed\-only" write; the form holding both the seed and the expanded key is rejected.

<a name="ParsePrivateKeyPEM"></a>
## func [ParsePrivateKeyPEM](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/pem.go#L311>)

```go
func ParsePrivateKeyPEM(keyPEM []byte) (key crypto.Signer, err error)
```

ParsePrivateKeyPEM parses and returns a PEM\-encoded private key. The private key may be either an unencrypted PKCS\#8, PKCS\#1, or elliptic private key.

<a name="ParsePrivateKeyPEMWithPassword"></a>
## func [ParsePrivateKeyPEMWithPassword](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/pem.go#L322>)

```go
func ParsePrivateKeyPEMWithPassword(keyPEM []byte, password []byte) (key crypto.Signer, err error)
```

ParsePrivateKeyPEMWithPassword parses and returns a PEM\-encoded private key. The private key may be an unencrypted PKCS\#8, PKCS\#1, or SEC1 key, a legacy PEM block encrypted per RFC 1423 \(Proc\-Type: 4,ENCRYPTED\), or an encrypted PKCS\#8 key \(ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY\) as described by GetKeyDERFromPEM. The key may be RSA, ECDSA, Ed25519 or ML\-DSA \(the last two PKCS\#8 only\). A nil password fails for an encrypted key; a wrong password returns an error that matches x509.IncorrectPasswordError.

<a name="ParsePublicKeyFromPEM"></a>
## func [ParsePublicKeyFromPEM](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/pem.go#L206>)

```go
func ParsePublicKeyFromPEM(key []byte) (crypto.PublicKey, error)
```

ParsePublicKeyFromPEM parses a PEM encoded public key in the SubjectPublicKeyInfo form \(RFC 5280\), or a PKCS\#1 RSA public key. It returns what x509.ParsePKIXPublicKey does, so any type that function supports, including \*ecdh.PublicKey and \*dsa.PublicKey, which cannot verify a modern signature: a caller that needs a signature key checks the type.

<a name="Bundle"></a>
## type [Bundle](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundle.go#L41-L56>)

A Bundle contains a certificate and its trust chain. It is intended to store the most widely applicable chain, with shortness an explicit goal.

```go
type Bundle struct {
    // Chain does not include the root anchor
    Chain       []*x509.Certificate
    Cert        *x509.Certificate
    IssuerCert  *x509.Certificate
    RootCert    *x509.Certificate
    Issuer      *pkix.Name
    Subject     *pkix.Name
    IssuerID    string
    SubjectID   string
    Expires     time.Time
    Hostnames   []string
    CertPEM     string
    CACertsPEM  string
    RootCertPEM string
}
```

<a name="SortBundlesByExpiration"></a>
### func [SortBundlesByExpiration](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundle.go#L197>)

```go
func SortBundlesByExpiration(bundles []*Bundle) []*Bundle
```

SortBundlesByExpiration returns a new slice of bundles sorted by Expires in descending order. The sort is stable, so bundles with the same Expires keep their input order, and nil bundles go last. The caller's slice is not reordered; the bundles themselves are shared \(XPKI\-038\).

<a name="Bundle.ExpiresInHours"></a>
### func \(\*Bundle\) [ExpiresInHours](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundle.go#L61>)

```go
func (b *Bundle) ExpiresInHours() time.Duration
```

ExpiresInHours returns the time until Expires truncated toward zero to whole hours: 90 minutes is 1h, and an expiry 90 minutes ago is \-1h \(XPKI\-045\).

<a name="BundleFlavor"></a>
## type [BundleFlavor](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L35>)

BundleFlavor is named optimization strategy on certificate chain selection when bundling.

```go
type BundleFlavor string
```

<a name="Optimal"></a>

```go
const (
    // Optimal means the shortest chain with newest intermediates and
    // the most advanced crypto.
    Optimal BundleFlavor = "optimal"

    // Force means the bundler only verifies the input as a valid bundle, not optimization is done.
    Force BundleFlavor = "force"
)
```

<a name="Bundler"></a>
## type [Bundler](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L69-L77>)

A Bundler contains the certificate pools for producing certificate bundles. It contains any intermediates and root certificates that should be used.

A Bundler is safe for concurrent use. Intermediates learned over AIA are shared by later calls: they are published by replacing the intermediate pool and the known issuers with updated copies, so a pool or map once read is never modified \(XPKI\-035\). RootPool, IntermediatePool, IsKnownIssuer and VerifyOptions read the current ones.

```go
type Bundler struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="LoadBundler"></a>
### func [LoadBundler](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L168>)

```go
func LoadBundler(rootBundleFile, intBundleFile string, opt ...Option) (*Bundler, error)
```

LoadBundler creates a new Bundler from the files passed in; these files should contain a list of valid root certificates and a list of valid intermediate certificates, respectively.

<a name="NewBundler"></a>
### func [NewBundler](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L222>)

```go
func NewBundler(roots, intermediates []*x509.Certificate, opt ...Option) (*Bundler, error)
```

NewBundler returns a Bundler that trusts roots, plus the system roots with WithSystemRoots, and uses intermediates to build chains. The flavor defaults to Optimal with trust roots and to Force without them; Optimal without trust roots is an error, so a Bundler never trusts system roots implicitly. The root pool is nil only when there are no trust roots.

<a name="NewBundlerFromPEM"></a>
### func [NewBundlerFromPEM](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L204>)

```go
func NewBundlerFromPEM(rootBundlePEM, intBundlePEM []byte, opt ...Option) (*Bundler, error)
```

NewBundlerFromPEM creates a new Bundler from PEM\-encoded root certificates and intermediate certificates. Without root certificates the default flavor is Force; see NewBundler.

<a name="Bundler.Bundle"></a>
### func \(\*Bundler\) [Bundle](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L721>)

```go
func (b *Bundler) Bundle(certs []*x509.Certificate, key crypto.Signer) (*Chain, error)
```

Bundle takes an X509 certificate \(already in the Certificate structure\), a private key as crypto.Signer in one of the appropriate formats \(i.e. \*rsa.PrivateKey, \*ecdsa.PrivateKey or \*mldsa.PrivateKey, or even an opaque key\), using them to build a certificate bundle. certs\[0\] is the leaf \(a reversed chain is detected\); its key must be RSA, ECDSA or ML\-DSA. A nil or empty certs returns an error matching ErrNoCertificates, and a nil entry returns an error \(XPKI\-036\).

<a name="Bundler.BundleContext"></a>
### func \(\*Bundler\) [BundleContext](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L729>)

```go
func (b *Bundler) BundleContext(ctx context.Context, certs []*x509.Certificate, key crypto.Signer) (*Chain, error)
```

BundleContext is Bundle with a context that bounds and cancels AIA downloads. When ctx is done during an AIA download, the returned error matches ctx.Err\(\) with errors.Is. An Optimal Bundler without trust roots fails instead of verifying against the system roots.

<a name="Bundler.ChainFromFile"></a>

```go
func (b *Bundler) ChainFromFile(bundleFile, keyFile string, password string) (*Chain, error)
```

ChainFromFile takes a set of files containing the PEM\-encoded leaf certificate \(optionally along with some intermediate certs\), the PEM\-encoded private key and returns the bundle built from that key and the certificate\(s\).

<a name="Bundler.ChainFromPEM"></a>
### func \(\*Bundler\) [ChainFromPEM](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L364>)

```go
func (b *Bundler) ChainFromPEM(certsRaw, keyPEM []byte, password string) (*Chain, error)
```

ChainFromPEM builds a certificate chain from the set of byte slices containing the PEM or DER\-encoded certificate\(s\), private key.

<a name="Bundler.ChainFromPEMContext"></a>
### func \(\*Bundler\) [ChainFromPEMContext](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L370>)

```go
func (b *Bundler) ChainFromPEMContext(ctx context.Context, certsRaw, keyPEM []byte, password string) (*Chain, error)
```

ChainFromPEMContext is ChainFromPEM with a context that bounds and cancels AIA downloads; see BundleContext.

<a name="Bundler.IntermediatePool"></a>
### func \(\*Bundler\) [IntermediatePool](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L88>)

```go
func (b *Bundler) IntermediatePool() *x509.CertPool
```

IntermediatePool returns a copy of the intermediates known now: those the Bundler was created with and those it has learned over AIA since.


<a name="Bundler.RootPool"></a>
### func \(\*Bundler\) [RootPool](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L81>)

```go
func (b *Bundler) RootPool() *x509.CertPool
```

<a name="Bundler.VerifyOptions"></a>
### func \(\*Bundler\) [VerifyOptions](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L277>)

```go
func (b *Bundler) VerifyOptions() x509.VerifyOptions
```

VerifyOptions returns the x509.VerifyOptions used by Optimal bundling. Roots is never nil: without trust roots it is an empty pool, so the options never fall back to the system roots. It is a snapshot: intermediates learned later are not added to it.

<a name="Chain"></a>
## type [Chain](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L674-L685>)

Chain contains a certificate and its trust chain. It is intended to store the most widely applicable chain, with shortness an explicit goal.

```go
type Chain struct {
    Chain       []*x509.Certificate

    Key         any

```

<a name="KeyInfo"></a>
## type [KeyInfo](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/keyinfo.go#L19-L25>)

KeyInfo provides information about the key: Type is KeyTypeRSA, KeyTypeECDSA or KeyTypeMLDSA; KeySize is the RSA modulus or ECDSA curve size in bits, or the ML\-DSA parameter set number \(44, 65 or 87\); Hash is the digest a hash\-then\-sign caller uses with the key, and zero for an ML\-DSA key, which signs the message itself.

```go
type KeyInfo struct {
    KeySize   int
    Type      string
    IsPrivate bool
    Hash      crypto.Hash
    Key       any
}
```

<a name="NewKeyInfo"></a>
### func [NewKeyInfo](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/keyinfo.go#L31>)

```go
func NewKeyInfo(k any) (*KeyInfo, error)
```

NewKeyInfo returns the KeyInfo of k: an RSA, ECDSA or ML\-DSA private key, public key, crypto.Signer or crypto.Decrypter \(an HSM or KMS key, whose Public\(\) is inspected\) or a JWK holding one of them. IsPrivate is set only for an in\-memory private key.

<a name="Option"></a>
## type [Option](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L119>)

An Option sets options such as allowed key usages, etc.

```go
type Option func(*options)
```

<a name="WithAIA"></a>
### func [WithAIA](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L140>)

```go
func WithAIA(enable bool) Option
```

WithAIA lets to enable downloading issuers from AIA.

<a name="WithBundleFlavor"></a>
### func [WithBundleFlavor](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L133>)

```go
func WithBundleFlavor(flavor BundleFlavor) Option
```

WithBundleFlavor selects Optimal or Force chain building. Without this option the flavor is Optimal when the Bundler has trust roots \(explicit roots or WithSystemRoots\) and Force otherwise. NewBundler rejects Optimal without trust roots and any other flavor value; the last option wins.

<a name="WithHTTPClient"></a>
### func [WithHTTPClient](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L159>)

```go
func WithHTTPClient(client *http.Client) Option
```

WithHTTPClient sets the client for AIA downloads. Each request is bounded by the client's Timeout, or 3s when it is zero, and by the context given to BundleContext. Only a 200 response of at most 1 MiB is parsed. Without this option a client with a 3s timeout is used.

<a name="WithKeyUsages"></a>
### func [WithKeyUsages](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L123>)

```go
func WithKeyUsages(usages ...x509.ExtKeyUsage) Option
```

WithKeyUsages lets you set which Extended Key Usage values are acceptable. By default x509.ExtKeyUsageAny will be used.

<a name="WithSystemRoots"></a>
### func [WithSystemRoots](<https://github.com/effective-security/xpki/blob/main/certutil/bundler.go#L149>)

```go
func WithSystemRoots(enable bool) Option
```

WithSystemRoots adds the platform trust store \(x509.SystemCertPool\) to the explicit roots. It is the only way a Bundler trusts system roots: without it, Optimal verification uses the explicit roots alone \(XPKI\-041\).
